lead: Silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN) have a band gap about three times that of silicon. A wider gap means a much higher critical electric field, so a thin, heavily doped drift layer can block the same voltage. That gives far lower on-resistance at a given rating, fast unipolar switching at high voltage, and operation at higher temperature. SiC MOSFETs now replace IGBTs in 800 V electric-vehicle inverters and solar inverters; GaN transistors fill laptop and phone fast chargers and server supplies.
prereq: You need: the power MOSFET, its R<sub>DS(on)</sub> and gate charge, from the BJT, MOSFET and IGBT chapter.

sections.h3: Why a wide band gap helps

blocks.text: The band gap E<sub>g</sub> is the energy needed to free an electron from the valence band into the conduction band, in electron-volts (eV). Silicon has about 1.1 eV, 4H-SiC about 3.3 eV and GaN about 3.4 eV. A wider gap makes avalanche breakdown need a much stronger field: the critical field E<sub>c</sub> is about 0.3 MV/cm in silicon, about 2.2 MV/cm in SiC and about 3 MV/cm in GaN (1 MV/cm = 10<sup>6</sup> V/cm).
where W<sub>drift</sub> is the drift-layer thickness (cm), V<sub>B</sub> the blocking voltage (V) and E<sub>c</sub> the critical field in V/cm, for a triangular field profile.

A thinner drift layer that can also be doped more heavily has much lower resistance. The ideal specific on-resistance of the drift region is 4 V<sub>B</sub>² / (ε μ E<sub>c</sub>³), so the material quality is ranked by ε μ E<sub>c</sub>³, the Baliga figure of merit (ε is permittivity, μ electron mobility). Because E<sub>c</sub> is cubed, SiC and GaN beat silicon by hundreds of times. SiC also conducts heat two to three times better than silicon, so heat leaves the die easily; GaN is closer to silicon.

A SiC MOSFET is a vertical device like a silicon power MOSFET, with the drain at the bottom. It is normally off, made from 650 V to 3.3 kV, and usually driven at +15 V to +20 V on and 0 V to −5 V off; the gate oxide does not tolerate overshoot beyond the datasheet limits. Its body diode works but has a forward drop of about 3 V and a small Q<sub>rr</sub>.

A GaN HEMT (high electron mobility transistor) is lateral: source, gate and drain are on the top surface. An AlGaN layer on GaN forms a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG), a thin sheet of very mobile electrons that is the channel. Power GaN parts are mostly enhancement-mode (normally off), rated up to about 650 V. The gate tolerates only about +6 V to +7 V, so drives are tight. GaN has no p-n body diode: in reverse the channel itself conducts, with a drop of a few volts, and there is no reverse recovery charge.

items: Datasheet lines to read: maximum V<sub>GS</sub>; R<sub>DS(on)</sub> at 25 °C and at high temperature; Q<sub>g</sub> and Q<sub>rr</sub>; C<sub>oss</sub>; Rθ<sub>JC</sub>.

sections.h3: Switching, losses and where each is used

blocks.text: Both are unipolar devices, so there is no tail current, and their small capacitances and gate charge allow switching at 100 kHz to several megahertz. Gate drive loss is P<sub>gate</sub> = Q<sub>g</sub> V<sub>drive</sub> f<sub>s</sub>. The price is very fast edges, tens of volts per nanosecond, which push current through every parasitic capacitance and make ringing, interference and false turn-on likely unless the layout is tight.

blocks.text: At 1200 V a SiC MOSFET can replace an IGBT and switch several times faster, which shrinks inductors and filters; at 650 V and below GaN competes with silicon superjunction MOSFETs in compact high-frequency supplies.

examples.question: A SiC MOSFET has R<sub>DS(on)</sub> = 20 mΩ and a silicon MOSFET of the same voltage rating 100 mΩ. Both carry 20 A rms. Find each conduction loss and their ratio.
examples.answer: P<sub>SiC</sub> = 8 W and P<sub>Si</sub> = 40 W: the silicon part loses five times as much.

examples.question: Estimate the drift-layer thickness needed to block 1200 V in silicon (E<sub>c</sub> = 0.3 MV/cm), SiC (2.2 MV/cm) and GaN (3 MV/cm).
steps: Silicon needs 80 ÷ 10.9 ≈ 7.3 times the SiC thickness, and its layer must also be far more lightly doped, so its resistance is much higher.
examples.answer: About 80 µm for Si, 10.9 µm for SiC and 8 µm for GaN.

traps: Putting E<sub>c</sub> in MV/cm into W = 2V<sub>B</sub>/E<sub>c</sub>: with 2.2 instead of 2.2 × 10<sup>6</sup> V/cm the 1200 V layer comes out as 1091 cm instead of 10.9 µm.
Wide band-gap devices are not drop-in replacements: a GaN gate tolerates only about 6 V, and SiC wants +15 V to +20 V.
GaN has no p-n body diode; reverse current flows in the channel with a drop of a few volts, but no Q<sub>rr</sub>.
R<sub>DS(on)</sub> rises with temperature in SiC and GaN too; use the hot value for losses.
Fast edges (tens of V/ns) cause ringing and false turn-on even when average currents and voltages look safe.

quiz.q: Give the approximate band gap and critical field of Si, SiC and GaN.
quiz.a: Si 1.1 eV, 0.3 MV/cm; SiC 3.3 eV, 2.2 MV/cm; GaN 3.4 eV, 3 MV/cm.

quiz.q: What is the 2DEG in a GaN HEMT?
quiz.a: A two-dimensional electron gas: a thin sheet of very mobile electrons at the AlGaN/GaN interface that forms the channel.

quiz.q: Why does a higher critical field give a lower on-resistance at the same voltage rating?
quiz.a: The drift layer can be thinner (W ≈ 2V<sub>B</sub>/E<sub>c</sub>) and more heavily doped, so it has less resistance; the ideal specific on-resistance falls as 1/E<sub>c</sub>³.

quiz.q: Why is a GaN HEMT called lateral and a SiC MOSFET vertical?
quiz.a: In GaN, source, gate and drain are on the top surface and current flows sideways in the 2DEG. In SiC the drain is at the bottom of the die and current flows vertically through the drift layer.

quiz.q: A GaN HEMT has Q<sub>g</sub> = 8 nC and is driven at 5 V and 200 kHz. Find the gate drive power.
A SiC MOSFET has R<sub>DS(on)</sub> = 25 mΩ at 25 °C and 40 mΩ at 125 °C. Find its conduction loss at 15 A at both temperatures.
A SiC MOSFET switches 400 V in 10 ns. Find dv/dt and the current it drives through a 50 pF stray capacitance.
quiz.a: dv/dt = 400 V ÷ 10 ns = 40 V/ns = 4 × 10<sup>10</sup> V/s; i = C dv/dt = 50 × 10<sup>−12</sup> × 4 × 10<sup>10</sup> = 2 A, enough to cause ringing and false triggering.

quiz.q: A silicon MOSFET's gate drive is reused for a GaN HEMT and the GaN gate fails. Give two likely reasons.
quiz.a: The 10 V to 12 V drive exceeds the GaN gate limit of about 6 V; and gate ringing from the faster switching and the old layout adds overshoot above the limit.

beyond: Not for the exam. 800 V electric-vehicle traction inverters use SiC MOSFET modules, and GaN is moving from chargers to motor drives and data-centre supplies. Research topics include trench SiC MOSFETs, GaN-on-silicon reliability, dynamic R<sub>DS(on)</sub> in GaN and gallium oxide, a still wider gap material. Search for ‘Baliga figure of merit’, ‘GaN HEMT 2DEG’ and ‘SiC MOSFET gate oxide reliability’.
